```python
def next_permutation(perm):
    for i in range(len(perm) - 2, -1, -1):
        if perm[i] < perm[i + 1]:
            for j in range(len(perm) - 1, i, -1):
                if perm[j] > perm[i]:  # The bug is fixed here
                    next_perm = list(perm)
                    next_perm[i], next_perm[j] = perm[j], perm[i]
                    next_perm[i + 1:] = reversed(next_perm[i + 1:])
                    return next_perm
```

- The code is trying to find the next lexicographic permutation of the given permutation `perm`.
- It starts by scanning from the right side of the permutation to find the first pair of adjacent elements where the left element is smaller than the right element. This indicates the point where the permutation needs to be modified to get the next permutation.
- Once the pair is found (index `i`), the code looks for the smallest element in the subarray `perm[i+1:]` that is greater than `perm[i]`. This is where the bug was occurring. The condition should be `perm[j] > perm[i]` to find the smallest element greater than `perm[i]`.
- After finding the appropriate element at index `j`, the code swaps `perm[i]` and `perm[j]`, and then reverses the subarray `perm[i+1:]` to get the next permutation.

With the corrected condition `if perm[j] > perm[i]`, the function will correctly find the next lexicographic permutation of the given permutation.
